page: Amazon Web Services r8a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated 16-core AMD EPYC 9R45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 1 thread per core and capable of reaching clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16) and cryptographic extensions. Paired with the compute core is 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage over an 8 Gbps baseline network link.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional per-core compute and memory efficiency. The single-core stress-ng score of 3,773.38 and single-core Geekbench score of 2,819.0 place the instance in the top tier, supported by top-tier gzip single-threaded compression (41.51 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (18.28 GB/sec). Multi-core Geekbench also reaches the top tier at 21,849.0, aided by strong PassMark memory performance (2,840.77) and large-block memory read bandwidth of 109.04 GB/sec. Parallelized integer-heavy tasks such as multi-core stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests fall in the middle tier, reflecting the total count of 16 threads.

In operational benchmarks, the instance demonstrates high static web serving throughput (53.16 GB/sec) and handles 54.9 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-based small LLM inference achieves top-tier text generation at 471.96 tokens per second, but throughput moderates to average tiers for 7B models (24.02 tokens/sec). With its high-frequency AMD EPYC silicon and 128 GB of DDR5 RAM, the r8a.4xlarge offers strong qualitative resource efficiency for memory-bound workloads, large in-memory caches, enterprise relational databases, real-time analytics engines, and data transformation pipelines that do not depend on local ephemeral storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a 16-core AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with dedicated execution threads running up to 4.5 GHz, supported by 128.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory at an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration has no integrated GPU, no local ephemeral storage, and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. In benchmarks, it exhibits top-tier single-core performance, top-tier Geekbench multi-core throughput, and strong memory and data compression capabilities. While multi-threaded throughput on dense parallel tasks remains in the middle tier due to the 16-thread profile, its high memory bandwidth and DDR5 capacity make it an efficient deployment choice for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise analytics, and data pipeline processing.
